notes: Real SplitEdge component and point clicks, public Rhino APIs/commands, actual Undo/Redo and prompt-time camera calibration run in an owned private Xvfb session. User desktops and existing Rhino sessions were not used.

The 30-case initial diagnostic was followed by a fresh 44-case run adding elevated polygon NURBS, repeated and collinear loops, warped and subdivided surfaces and two coordinate-permuted nonplanar polygons. Only the final response is retained as a replay fixture.
Portable requests replace the shared box artifact path with its source recipe. Response values are compacted as JSON without numerical normalization or array reordering.
Each family has one-shot Cen over all five persistent modes and persistent Cen-only. Open, nearly closed, empty-center, surface-interior and warped-surface controls are admission-only misses.

Native queries use the recorded world-to-screen matrix, actual click pixel and 12-pixel capture radius. Captured native points, never Rhino output positions, drive command replay at absolute 1e-9 and relative 1e-10.

The original subdivided-surface target x=4.5 remains in the requests. The actual corner-average target is x=4.75 because collinear subdivisions within straight surface edges are not additional corners. Native replay computes the target from geometry.

The nonplanar polyline captures disagree with a planar-only reading of the Rhino help page. Separate coordinate permutations constrain its x, y and z mean components via the resulting SplitEdge x coordinate; no direct unconstrained GetPoint output is claimed.

The subdivided surface exposed native natural-trim parameter domains of [0,1] instead of the corresponding surface interval. OpenNURBS NewOuterLoop independently confirms the native-interval construction rule.
General conic recognition, occlusion, arbitrary camera/priority parity, high-degree or mixed-sign rational completeness and cross-engine performance remain unproved.
